Domains.name: CAS Number
Domains.description:
A CAS Registry Number is a unique and unambiguous identifier for a specific substance that allows clear communication and, with the help of CAS scientists, links together all available data and research about that substance. Governmental agencies rely on CAS Registry Numbers for substance identification in regulatory applications because they are unique, easy validated, and internationally recognized.

Each CAS Registry Number (CAS RN) identifier:

Domains.name: Index Number CLP Annex VI Tab 3
Domains.description:
The index number is a European Union identifier for a specific hazardous substance. The list of index numbers was originally listed in Annex I to Directive 67/548/EEC[1] and is now in Annex VI to Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP)[2]. It is regularly adapted to technical progress.

The index number must be distinguished from the EC number.
The index number of the individual substances consists of a character sequence according to the pattern ABC-RST-VW-Y.

ABC identifies the element or organic group that is most characteristic for the properties of the substance. For elements, their atomic number is used; organic substances are grouped into classes due to their diversity, with each class being assigned a number.
RST is the consecutive number of the substance in the ABC series.
VW indicates the form in which the substance is manufactured or placed on the market.
Y is the control number, which is calculated using the ten-digit ISBN method.

Domains.name: Latitude
Domains.description:
Latitude is a measurement of a location north or south of the Equator. Lines of latitude (also called parallels) are imaginary lines that circle Earth’s surface, running east and west parallel to the Equator. It is measured in degrees (°), which may be broken down into smaller units called minutes (′) and seconds (″). It can also be expressed in decimal degrees; negative values of decimal degrees represent latitudes in the Southern Hemisphere and longitudes in the Western Hemisphere.
Lines of latitude north of the Equator (the line that marks 0° latitude) are numbered from 1° to 89° N, and those south of the Equator are numbered from 1° to 89° S."

Granularity with 5 decimals is approx. to 1 meter.

Can be displayed as a decimal number 30.14402˚ , -30.14402 or 30.14402˚ N, 30.14402 N or with degrees minutes and seconds 30˚ 2‘ 12’ N or 30˚ 5‘ 34.113’ S or in  a short form  4626N (degrees, minutes, N/S)

additionalProps.Description:de:
Der Breitengrad ist ein Maß für einen Ort nördlich oder südlich des Äquators. Breitengradlinien (auch Parallelen genannt) sind imaginäre Linien, die die Erdoberfläche umkreisen und parallel zum Äquator nach Osten und Westen verlaufen. Er wird in Grad (°) gemessen, die in kleinere Einheiten, die Minuten (′) und Sekunden (″), unterteilt werden können. Er kann auch in Dezimalgraden ausgedrückt werden; negative Werte von Dezimalgraden stehen für Breitengrade in der südlichen Hemisphäre und für Längengrade in der westlichen Hemisphäre.
Die Breitengrade nördlich des Äquators (die Linie, die den 0. Breitengrad markiert) sind von 1° bis 89° N nummeriert, die südlich des Äquators von 1° bis 89° S.“

Die Granularität mit 5 Dezimalstellen entspricht ca. 1 Meter.

Kann als Dezimalzahl 30.14402˚ , -30.14402 oder 30.14402˚ N, 30.14402 N oder mit Grad Minuten und Sekunden 30˚ 2' 12' N oder 30˚ 5' 34.113' S angezeigt werden.

Domains.name: Longitude
Domains.description:
Lines of longitude (also called meridians) run between the geographic North Pole and the geographic South Pole and are used to measure distances from the prime meridian. It is measured in degrees (°), which may be broken down into smaller units called minutes (′) and seconds (″). It can also be expressed in decimal degrees; negative values of decimal degrees represent latitudes in the Southern Hemisphere and longitudes in the Western Hemisphere. Lines of longitude east of the prime meridian (the line that marks 0° longitude) are numbered from 1° to 179° east (E). Lines of longitude west of the prime meridian are numbered from 1° to 179° west (W).

5 decimals result in a granularity of approx. 1 meter.

Can be displayed as a decimal number 30.14402˚ , -30.14402 or 30.14402˚ W, -30.14402 E or with degrees minutes and seconds 30˚ 2‘ 12’ W or 30˚ 5‘ 34.113’ E or in a short form  00612E (degree, minutes, W/E)

additionalProps.Description:de:
Die Längengrade (auch Meridiane genannt) verlaufen zwischen dem geografischen Nordpol und dem geografischen Südpol und werden zur Messung von Entfernungen vom Nullmeridian verwendet. Er wird in Grad (°) gemessen, die in kleinere Einheiten, die Minuten (′) und Sekunden (″), unterteilt werden können. Er kann auch in Dezimalgraden ausgedrückt werden; negative Werte von Dezimalgraden stehen für Breitengrade auf der Südhalbkugel und für Längengrade auf der Westhalbkugel. Die Längengrade östlich des Nullmeridians (die Linie, die den 0. Längengrad markiert) sind von 1° bis 179° Ost (E) nummeriert. Die Längengrade westlich des Nullmeridians sind von 1° bis 179° West (W) nummeriert.

5 Dezimalstellen ergeben eine Granularität von ca. 1 Meter.

Kann als Dezimalzahl 30.14402˚ , -30.14402 oder 30.14402˚ W, -30.14402 E oder mit Grad, Minuten und Sekunden angezeigt werden 30˚ 2' 12' W oder 30˚ 5' 34.113' E

Methodological:
 - Access to new Emission Factor data (database, supplier-specific, company-specific)
 - Updated upstream data (i.e. upstream supplier updated their PCF based on methodology change)

Production Process:
 - Change in process
 - Change in feedstock
 - Change from conventional to certified sustainable material
 - Change in energy source
 - Change in upstream supplier
 - Updated upstream data (i.e. upstream supplier updated their PCF based on process change)

 3. Additional information on biogenic emissions & removals calculation  should be specified. Attributes.name: Latitude
Attributes.description:
Latitude is a measurement of a location north or south of the Equator. Lines of latitude (also called parallels) are imaginary lines that circle Earth’s surface, running east and west parallel to the Equator. It is measured in degrees (°), which may be broken down into smaller units called minutes (′) and seconds (″). It can also be expressed in decimal degrees; negative values of decimal degrees represent latitudes in the Southern Hemisphere and longitudes in the Western Hemisphere.
Lines of latitude north of the Equator (the line that marks 0° latitude) are numbered from 1° to 89° N, and those south of the Equator are numbered from 1° to 89° S.

Attributes.name: Longitude
Attributes.description: Lines of longitude (also called meridians) run between the geographic North Pole and the geographic South Pole and are used to measure distances from the prime meridian. It is measured in degrees (°), which may be broken down into smaller units called minutes (′) and seconds (″). It can also be expressed in decimal degrees; negative values of decimal degrees represent latitudes in the Southern Hemisphere and longitudes in the Western Hemisphere. Lines of longitude east of the prime meridian (the line that marks 0° longitude) are numbered from 1° to 179° east (E). Lines of longitude west of the prime meridian are numbered from 1° to 179° west (W).
